Above the text block, a circular engraved medallion with a portrait and a legend around it, and Hebrew letters on either side of the head. Below the medallion, one block of text in full width. At the foot right, the signature.

main_text.p: CHRISTVS REX VENIT IN PACE DEVS HOMO FACTVS EST. [illegible, ~3 letters] [illegible, ~3 letters]

IESVS Christus Dominus noster, verus Deus ac verus homo,natus ex muliere virgine,factus sub lege, vt eos qui sub lege erant redimeret,passus est, mortémque in cruce pro vita & salute noftra oppetiit anno suae aetatis 33. anno mundi 3994. anno imperij Tiberij 18. ac post tres dies resurrexit, nempe vt qui mortem noftram moriendo destuxerat[?], vitam quoque re-surgendo repararet:mortuus est enim propter peccata noftra, & resurrexit propter iustificationem noftram : vt nos peccatis mortui,iustitiae viuamus,per bona opera certam facientes vo-cationem noftram. Quadragesimo autem die à morte ascedit in coelum:quinquagesimo, misit spiritum sanctum, quemadmodum suis fuerat pollicitus:& venturus est iudicare viuos & mortuos in consummatione seculi:beati serui illi quos paratos & vigilantes offendet. Euangelia,epistolae D.Pauli,Petri,Ioan-nis,Iacobi proponunt nobis ob oculos isthaec omnia, Christi vitam, mortem, resurrectionem, ascensionem, spiritus sancti missionem, mundi conflagrationem extremam,extremum quo-que venturi eiusdem Christi iudicium, vitam aeternam, & sup-plicium aeternum.

page.notes: Engraving: a circular medallion with a bust portrait of Christ in profile facing right, long hair and beard, with a cloak. The legend around the rim reads CHRISTVS REX VENIT IN PACE DEVS HOMO FACTVS EST, with the words running clockwise. The Hebrew letters beside the head are not legible on the scan and are marked illegible. Doubtful reading: "destuxerat" is marked [?]; the letter form is unclear on the scan and may be "destruxerat". Printing errors left as printed: "suis" for "suis", "extremu" for "extremum" in the line "extremū quo-que", "3994" as printed, "fuerat pollicitus:&" with the colon. Other spellings such as "ascedit" and "resurrexit" are as printed.
